q: How many bits are in one IPv6 hextet?
explain: A hextet is four hex digits, and each digit is 4 bits: 4 × 4 = 16.

q: How many hextets make up a full IPv6 address?
explain: 128 bits divided into 16-bit groups gives 8 hextets.

q: What is 0db8 in binary?
explain: 0 = 0000, d = 1101, b = 1011, 8 = 1000. Keep the leading 0000 so all 16 bits line up.

q: Why do IPv6 addresses use hexadecimal instead of binary or dotted decimal?
opts: Hex shortens 128 bits to 32 characters and maps exactly to 4-bit groups
Hex values are larger than binary values
explain: Every hex digit stands for exactly four bits, so 128 bits fit in 32 readable characters with no math lost.
